title: Prove DPM app-hiding persists, and build the enforcement decision layer on it
objective: The Device Owner design rests on setApplicationHidden surviving a reboot, which had never been tested - both shell primitives were measured to be cleared by one. Prove or disprove that WITHOUT spending a factory reset, then build the decision layer that turns the parsed policy plus current conditions into a hide/show set. Success is a measured persistence result with its scope stated honestly, and a pure, fully tested decision function.
acceptance_criteria: setApplicationHidden persistence measured across a real reboot, using a removable managed profile so no wipe is spent
The test profile and its profile-owner grant are removed afterwards, with user 0 verified untouched
The result is recorded with its scope limit: profile owner in a work profile is NOT device owner in user 0
EnforcementDecision is a pure function of its inputs - testable with no device, clock or location provider
packagesToShow is always the complete allowed set rather than a delta, so a missed run self-repairs
Unknown location enforces rather than releasing, matching focus_daemon.sh
A policy with redacted coordinates still enforces rather than reading as always-away
Geofence hysteresis prevents flapping between radius and radius+hysteresis
The workout exception releases the YouTube packages and nothing else
Workout signal sources are verified on-device before being built, not assumed
out_of_scope: Device Owner provisioning and the factory reset - unchanged, still not done
The foreground service, BOOT_COMPLETED receiver and alarm scheduling - next step
com.kuhy.workout_app as a signal source: verified to expose nothing readable
org.runnerup: not installed on this device
verifier: pm create-user/dpm set-profile-owner + adb reboot + dumpsys package, then pm remove-user and re-check user 0; cd focus_owner && flutter analyze && flutter test
